pass_2.locations: Original Rooijers 2019 PMC6609448 JATS lines 99–113, especially “DamID adapters”, “CEL-Seq primers”, and “Raw data preprocessing”; original source-bundle scraper
pass_2.finding: Methods specify DpnI digestion, adapter ligation, pooled T7 IVT and CEL-Seq2-derived RT; the DamID adapter paragraph distinguishes a four-base fork from a six-base Dam-RING1B mESC variant. pass_1.finding: Independently verified CEL-Seq2 retains barcoded oligo(dT) RT and IVT but shortens its own RT primer from 92 to 82 nt by reducing the cell barcode from eight to six bases despite adding a six-base UMI. scDam&T uses its own published split eight-base barcode and should not inherit the predecessor length.

pass_2.finding: CEL-Seq2 introduced barcoded oligo(dT) RT with IVT amplification and optimized its own RT primer from 92 to 82 bases by shortening the barcode from eight to six bases. scDam&T-seq adapts this architecture but its own 2019 article and 2020 detailed protocol explicitly print split eight-base RNA barcodes. Predecessor does not establish scDam&T-seq member assignments.

pass_2.finding: Followed the RNA predecessor and later detailed protocol independently. conclusion: Two independent readers checked the 2019 article, original oligo tables, author preprint, 2020 detailed protocol and CEL-Seq2 predecessor. The page scopes its six-base-fork drawing to the later detailed example and distinguishes the original four-base-fork variant. Exact 2019 experiment-to-primer-member assignments remain unresolved; no absence claim is accepted.
